research_mode: official primary sources only; police open-data, ONS crime methodology and Home Office outcome-methodology gates; no parcel result, local risk score or business result claimed

sources.name: Crime-outcomes reporting period
verified_claims: The 2025 to 2026 bulletin covers investigative outcomes assigned to notifiable offences recorded between 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026.
limitations: The reporting period is not the same as the date every investigation closed or outcome was assigned.

sources.name: Crime-outcomes force coverage
verified_claims: The bulletin covers all territorial police forces in England and Wales and British Transport Police.
limitations: Coverage does not guarantee identical data quality or system capability across forces.

sources.name: Crime-outcomes framework origin
verified_claims: The current crime outcomes framework replaced the narrower detections framework introduced before 2013.
limitations: Historical detection and current outcome measures should not be treated as directly interchangeable.

sources.name: Quarterly outcomes tables
verified_claims: The Home Office publishes quarterly crime-outcomes tables without commentary in addition to the annual bulletin.
limitations: Quarterly tables may be revised and should not be read without definitions and technical notes.

sources.name: Victim and non-victim offence split
verified_claims: The bulletin separates victim-based offences from non-victim-based offences because their nature and outcome timeliness differ.
limitations: The broad split does not replace offence-level analysis.

sources.name: Outcome variation factors
verified_claims: Crime outcomes vary by offence nature, evidence availability, victim or witness engagement and investigative complexity.
limitations: Differences in outcome rates must not be treated as a direct standalone measure of force effectiveness.

sources.name: Year-end case-status snapshot
verified_claims: The main recorded-crime data is a snapshot of the current case status at the time of analysis.
limitations: Snapshot status is provisional for open or complex investigations.

sources.name: Subsequent outcome revisions
verified_claims: Outcomes can be revised in later releases as investigations finish or new lines of enquiry open.
limitations: Previously published outcomes must not be assumed final.

sources.name: Open-investigation interpretation
verified_claims: Where many investigations remain open, first-published data does not provide a complete picture of police performance.
limitations: Open-case proportions require maturity and follow-up analysis.

sources.name: Grouped outcomes and open-data transparency
verified_claims: The bulletin groups outcomes for presentation while separate open-data tables provide the full range of outcome types.
limitations: Grouped categories can hide material distinctions and should not replace detailed outcome codes.

sources.name: One statistical outcome per crime
verified_claims: For statistical purposes, each recorded crime is assigned one outcome type under the counting rules.
limitations: The statistical outcome does not necessarily summarise every investigative or court event.

sources.name: Alternative-offence outcome publication
verified_claims: Outcome types 1a, 2a and 3a have been included in open and summary tables since late 2023 after Home Office quality assurance.
limitations: Publication after quality assurance does not identify the specific alternative offence in each case.

sources.name: Fraud data transition exclusion
verified_claims: The 2025 to 2026 bulletin excludes the usual fraud and computer-misuse chapter while City of London Police transitions from Action Fraud and NFIB systems to Report Fraud.
limitations: The omission must not be interpreted as zero fraud, no outcomes or a complete all-crime bulletin.

sources.name: Weapon-enabled offence subset
verified_claims: Firearm and knife or sharp-instrument offences are subsets of other offence categories rather than distinct offence categories.
limitations: Weapon-enabled counts must not be added again to their parent offence totals.

sources.name: Outcomes for offences recorded in period
verified_claims: The principal measure follows offences recorded in the reporting period and shows their outcome distribution.
limitations: At first publication some offences have no final assigned outcome and later tables revise the distribution.

sources.name: Outcomes closed in period
verified_claims: The closed-investigation measure includes outcomes assigned in the period regardless of when the associated crime was recorded.
limitations: It can include crimes from earlier years and is not a cohort outcome rate for the same recorded offences.

sources.name: Outcomes-to-crimes ratio caution
verified_claims: Comparing outcomes recorded in a year with crimes recorded in the same year can produce rates over 100 percent for low-volume crimes because the populations differ.
limitations: Such ratios must not be interpreted as a probability or cohort clearance rate.

sources.name: Alternative charged offence limitation
verified_claims: Home Office central data cannot identify the specific alternative offence charged when an alternative-offence outcome is recorded.
limitations: The alternative charge must not be inferred from the original offence category.

sources.name: Victim-based table fraud exclusion
verified_claims: Victim-based outcome tables exclude fraud offences recorded centrally through the national fraud system rather than territorial forces.
limitations: The victim-based totals are not complete totals for all victimisation offences.

sources.name: Outcome-timeliness data boundary
verified_claims: Median outcome-timeliness measures include only forces supplying record-level data to the Home Office Data Hub.
limitations: Timeliness statistics must not be assumed to cover every force or every outcome record uniformly.
